# <span id="aanchor349"></span> <span id="aanchor350"></span> System Configuration

[&lt;&lt; Back](System%20Configuration.md) \| [General](System%20Configuration.md) \| [Approvals](System%20Configuration%20-%20Approvals%20Tab.md) \| <a href="#" class="selected">Thresholds</a>

## Thresholds Tab

When the PPA options on the Approvals tab are set to "Approval Required", all PPAs must be approved before being applied. You can use the Thresholds tab to set limits so that approvals are required for edits to open months as well. When these limits are exceeded, approval is required before the edit can be applied.

Edits on open data that do not exceed the specified limits will apply immediately.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 626;height: 548;" />

The Thresholds tab contains the following options:

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="PPA Thresholds">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />PPA Thresholds</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="PPA Thresholds">

These parameters designate system-level minimum thresholds for PPAs when PPAs require approval. A PPA will be set to "Pending" if the PPA amount is equal to or greater than the Unit Diff. and the Percent Diff. values. Otherwise, the PPA will be rejected automatically and a meter message (number 705) will be logged. The rejected PPA can then be manually unrejected and approved from the [Edit Approvals](../../../Edit%20Approvals/Edit%20Approvals.md) screen.

FLOWCAL will first look to see if thresholds have been set at the meter level under Operational and Contractual Limits. If meter-level thresholds have not been set, system-level thresholds will be enforced. Gas meters will validate against the Gas Volume and Energy thresholds. Liquid meters will validate against the Mass, GSV and Summed Vol. thresholds.

The thresholds will only be enforced if the "Approval Required" PPA Option is selected in System Configuration. VCF edits, which are sometimes used to correct data values shown on final reports, do not alter volume but are still saved as PPAs. Such PPAs will be automatically rejected if the thresholds have been set and will need special attention by the user. Operational and Contractual limits require FLOWCAL Enterprise or the Master Characteristics module.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Monthly Edit Limit - Gas">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Monthly Edit Limits (Gas)*</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Monthly Edit Limit - Gas">

This is the limit at which accumulated edits made to gas volume or energy data for a gas meter during an open month require approval. Quality source apply and auto edits are not considered during calculation if edits have exceeded the edit approval limit.

<div class="example">

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example-Monthly Edit">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

If the edit limit is 1,000 units, an edit of 950 units will not require approval. However, if a subsequent edit of 60 units is made, the total edit amount exceeds the 1,000-unit limit (950 + 60 = 1010), so the edit of 60 units would require approval. This prevents original quantities from being altered non-typically without manager review.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Monthly Edit Limit - Liquids">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Monthly Edit Limits (Liquids)*</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Monthly Edit Limit - Liquids">

This is the limit at which accumulated edits made to GSV or mass data for a liquid meter during an open month require approval. Quality source apply and auto edits are not considered during calculation if edits have exceeded the edit approval limit.

<div class="example">

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example-Monthly Edit Liquids">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

If the edit limit is 1,000 units, an edit of 950 units will not require approval. However, if a subsequent edit of 60 units is made, the total edit amount exceeds the 1,000-unit limit (950 + 60 = 1010), so the edit of 60 units would require approval. This prevents original quantities from being altered non-typically without manager review.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Calibration Adjustments">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Calibration Adjustments - Gross Trip Point %</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Calibration Adjustments">

This is the allowable limit of error per transmitter in a TESTit test report. If the error for a particular transmitter exceeds this limit, an exception will be generated. This process is especially helpful in flagging potential erroneous data on test reports.

This feature requires TESTit 2 Integrated.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Max PPA Time Frame">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Max PPA Time Frame</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Max PPA Time Frame">

This is the system-level maximum time frame beyond which PPAs will automatically be rejected.

<div class="example">

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example-Max PPA">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

The threshold has been set to six months. In August 2018, a PPA is made to the closed production month of January 2018. The difference between the production month and the current business month is seven months, which is greater than the threshold, so the PPA will be rejected automatically.

</div>

</div>
